boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Mississippi, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daytime-to-game-day sequence of documented campus landmarks, study spaces, food, and culture for an under-21-safe first weekend.

cards.entity_name: Gertrude C. Ford Ole Miss Student Union
cards.title: Start at the Student Union
cards.subtitle: Campus hub • Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Use the Union as your first indoor waypoint: check the lobby, locate student-organization offices, and orient yourself before heading into the Grove.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for services, lounge areas, and student-life connections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gertrude C. Ford Ole Miss Student Union includes student-organization offices, lounge areas, a food court, and multipurpose space.
cards.source_title: The Gertrude C. Ford Ole Miss Student Union | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: The Union office lists weekday office hours of 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; building services may vary.

cards.title: Pick a low-pressure lunch stop
cards.subtitle: Student Union • Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Meet your group at the food court near the Grove, then choose from the listed counters instead of splitting up around campus on your first day.
cards.short_summary: A central meal stop with several familiar counter-service choices.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Union Food Court, located by the Grove, includes Chick-fil-A, Panda Express, Qdoba Mexican Grill, Blenz Bowls, and McAlister's Deli.
cards.access_notes: Food purchases are required; check Ole Miss Dining for current operating details.

cards.title: Walk through the Grove
cards.subtitle: Central campus • Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Take a daylight lap through the Grove from the Union side, note the stage and paths, and use the open space as a landmark for later meetups.
cards.short_summary: The campus green at the center of many Ole Miss gameday traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss identifies the Grove as the setting for gameday traditions including the Walk of Champions and performances by the Pride of the South.
cards.source_title: Gamedays in the Grove | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: Use normal campus access rules; gameday setups and event operations can affect use of the area.

cards.title: Find the Walk of Champions arch
cards.subtitle: East side of the Grove • Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Locate the arch and trace the route toward the stadium so you know where to stand if your first weekend includes a home football game.
cards.short_summary: A documented pregame route connecting the Grove and Vaught-Hemingway Stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: Before every home football game, the team walks from the Walk of Champions arch on the east side of the Grove toward Vaught-Hemingway Stadium.
cards.source_title: Campus Culture and Traditions | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: The team walk is scheduled for home-game days; follow official athletics information for game-specific timing.

cards.title: Make the library your reset point
cards.subtitle: 1 Library Loop • Friday evening
cards.notes: Enter from the fountain side, locate the circulation desk, and choose a table or carrel for a quiet reset after your first round of introductions.
cards.short_summary: The main library supplies study seating, collections, and public visitor access.
cards.evidence_claim: J.D. Williams Library is the university's general library, with study spaces, collections, and a west-side circulation desk at its fountain-side entrance.
cards.access_notes: The Williams and Science Libraries are open to the public; consult the library calendar for current building hours.

cards.title: Pause at Phi Mu Fountain
cards.subtitle: Library quad • Saturday morning
cards.notes: Use the fountain as a clear outdoor rendezvous point between the library and Paris-Yates Chapel, then continue across the academic core together.
cards.short_summary: A named fountain anchoring the quad beside the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Phi Mu Fountain is the centerpiece of the quad between J.D. Williams Library and Paris-Yates Chapel and was donated by Phi Mu alumnae and friends.
cards.source_title: Campus Culture and Traditions | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; observe posted campus rules and do not enter the fountain.

cards.title: Read the Lyceum in context
cards.subtitle: Lyceum Circle • Saturday morning
cards.notes: Walk the exterior slowly and read the site as a historic campus landmark; notice its columns and the context of the university's documented past.
cards.short_summary: The historic administration building and a key stop for understanding campus history.
cards.evidence_claim: Completed in 1848, the Lyceum is the university's principal administration building; its front columns retain bullet marks from the violence surrounding James Meredith's 1962 enrollment.
cards.access_notes: Treat this as an exterior history stop; administrative offices are not a general visitor destination.

cards.title: See the University Museum
cards.subtitle: 412 University Avenue • Saturday midday
cards.notes: Set aside about an hour for the galleries and choose one collection or exhibition to discuss afterward; the museum provides a calm cultural change of pace.
cards.short_summary: An academic museum with art, artifacts, and rotating exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Mississippi Museum and Historic Houses holds collections including Southern folk art, Greek and Roman antiquities, scientific instruments, and American fine art.
cards.source_title: Museum and Historic Houses | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: Public museum hours are Tuesday–Friday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; it is closed Sunday and Monday.

cards.title: Walk the Rowan Oak grounds
cards.subtitle: William Faulkner's home • Saturday afternoon
cards.notes: Take a self-guided walk around the grounds and exterior, then decide whether the paid house interior fits your plans; keep the visit at an unhurried pace.
cards.short_summary: The free grounds around William Faulkner's historic home offer a literary landmark close to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The grounds at Rowan Oak, William Faulkner's home, are open without charge from dawn to dusk daily.
cards.access_notes: Grounds are open dawn to dusk daily. Interior house admission costs $5 and has separate hours.

cards.title: End with a home-game option
cards.subtitle: Game-day stop • Saturday
cards.notes: If there is a home football game, watch the Walk of Champions first and then head toward the stadium with your valid ticket and your group's meeting plan.
cards.short_summary: A conditional final stop for an official Ole Miss home-football weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: Ole Miss states that the football team walks through the Grove to Vaught-Hemingway Stadium before every home game.
cards.source_title: Gamedays in the Grove | Ole Miss
cards.access_notes: Only use this stop on a home-game weekend; stadium entry requires the applicable event ticket and adherence to venue policies.
